title: Santa Maria Formation, Brazil: some of the earliest dinosaurs
summary: Red mudstones around Santa Maria in southern Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul hold some of the oldest known dinosaurs, among them Staurikosaurus, Saturnalia, Pampadromaeus and Buriolestes. Zircon dating puts the formation near 233 million years ago, in the Carnian of the Late Triassic. Dinosaurs were small and made up only about 5% of the fossils; the animals lived by lakes and on floodplains of a river system.

uncertainty.note: Weighted mean U-Pb zircon date 233.23 ± 0.73 Ma (2σ) for the Santa Maria Formation (Langer et al. 2018); the Pesquisa FAPESP article calls 233 Ma a maximum age and gives the Carnian as 237–227 Ma. The formation spans a longer interval than this single date; the Janner site fauna may be somewhat younger (Pampadromaeus paper).

beats.caption: Santa Maria Formation rocks, zircon-dated to about 233 million years ago, form a band of roughly 250 km across central Rio Grande do Sul.
Early dinosaurs lived here, including Staurikosaurus, Saturnalia, Pampadromaeus and Buriolestes, among rhynchosaurs and cynodonts; dinosaurs were about 5% of fossils.
The dating ties these Brazilian sites to other early dinosaur localities, giving a framework for when dinosaurs appeared in western Pangea.
